mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weeks (-15.7 to -13.1 to -12.6 to -10.7). This own-series momentum reflects an entrenched recovery trend in discretionary mobility that should persist mechanically over the next four weeks absent a shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC increased monotonically over the last 4 weekly observations
failure_condition: Mean RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is lower than or equal to the mean over the last 28 days despite the prior 4-week monotonic uptrend.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL time has declined steadily (9.6 to 6.9) while WORKPLACES mobility has risen (-28.6 to -19.6), indicating households are spending less time at home and more time in structured out-of-home activity. Once RESIDENTIAL drops below its prior week for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES simultaneously rises, retail footfall should follow with a lag as routines normalize.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL declines week-on-week for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES simultaneously rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell each of the last 3 weeks while WORKPLACES rose each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to increase over the next 2 weeks despite RESIDENTIAL falling and WORKPLACES rising concurrently for two straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT (-51.0 to -45.6) and WORKPLACES (-28.6 to -19.6) have both improved concurrently, suggesting a synchronized commuter-driven recovery. When both series rise together, the combined restoration of commuting infrastructure use and office attendance compounds to lift retail footfall near transit hubs and workplaces beyond what either series predicts alone.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improved in each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over 4 weeks even though TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both continue to co-improve, falsifying the compounding interaction.

mechanism_narrative: As Sydney enters early summer (mid-November), outdoor park usage typically gives way to indoor and retail-based leisure (shopping, air-conditioned venues) ahead of the holiday season. PARKS has already declined sharply (-9.4 to -18.0) while RETAIL_REC rose, consistent with a seasonal substitution effect that should continue into the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from -9.4 to -18.0 while RETAIL_REC rose from -15.7 to -10.7 over the same period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC declines or stagnates over the next 2 weeks even as PARKS continues to fall, indicating no substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has accelerated recently, rising by more than 3 points in two of the last three weeks, consistent with eased office-attendance policy restrictions. If this acceleration continues, the resulting short-term surge in weekday office-adjacent foot traffic should produce a near-immediate uptick in RETAIL_REC within one week.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week increase exceeds 3 points for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose by 3.2 and 4.0 points in two of the last three weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 1 week following two consecutive weeks of WORKPLACES increases exceeding 3 points.

mechanism_narrative: The approach of the pre-Christmas shopping season in late November/December historically drives a structural increase in retail activity independent of pandemic-recovery dynamics. Combined with the observed decline in RESIDENTIAL time, this seasonal shopping effect should push RETAIL_REC higher over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:decision date 2021-11-15 immediately precedes the pre-Christmas shopping period
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise over the next 4 weeks despite proximity to the holiday shopping season, contradicting the seasonal uplift hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has remained essentially flat (6.3 to 7.4) even as RETAIL_REC accelerated sharply in the most recent week, suggesting essential-trip demand has saturated while discretionary retail growth may be outpacing sustainable consumer bandwidth. This mismatch predicts a short-term deceleration or reversal in RETAIL_REC as the novelty of reopening fades and consumer fatigue sets in.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM stayed within a 1.1-point band over 4 weeks while RETAIL_REC rose 1.9 points in the most recent week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next week despite flat GROCERY_PHARM, indicating no saturation effect.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility growth has stalled after an initial jump, rising only 4.7, -0.1, and 0.8 points in the last three weeks respectively, suggesting persistent capacity limits or caution around public transport under lingering policy restrictions. If this stall continues for two more weeks, commuter-linked retail recovery should plateau or reverse as transit-dependent shoppers remain constrained.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week change stays below 1 point for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT week-on-week changes were -0.1 and 0.8 points in the last two weeks
regime_hint: partial reopening with lingering transit capacity restrictions
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to rise over the next 2 weeks despite TRANSIT growth remaining below 1 point per week, contradicting the stalled-transit constraint hypothesis.
